name: termcanvas
//: Read the comment in .devcontainer/Dockerfile first. Containment here is a function of what is NOT mounted and NOT installed, so the mount list below is deliberately short. Before adding a mount, ask: does this need to be writable, does it carry a credential, and is there a path that does not require it? Adding a mount here is a security decision, not a convenience one.
//mounts-why: Six mounts, and each is deliberate. (1) the repo-scoped PAT, mounted to the same relative path it has on the host so git-askpass.sh needs no container-specific variant. NOT the ~/.config/jef directory — that would also expose the jefscad and pixel-world PATs. (2) msmtp config, read-only — the unsupervised mode sends exactly one summary email per run; this is the only outbound capability the container has. (3) and (4) the shared instruction files and the spend-cap script, read-only so the agent cannot edit the rules it is operating under. (5) the wiki, read-only: the agent reads the distilled kb fundamentals, other projects' pages when a decision has cross-project implications — but cannot write, because the wiki is the one tier where an undetected error compounds instead of being caught. Proposals go to notes/wiki-proposals/ and a human promotes them. NOT ~/.ssh (the personal key reaches every repo on the account, including the wiki), NOT ~/.config/lab-bot (the bot credential), NOT ~/.aws or ~/.azure, NOT the host tool directory, NOT the docker socket (this repo builds nothing locally).
//features: No docker-in-docker: termcanvas builds nothing locally and needs no image builds, so the container gets no docker capability at all.

remoteEnv.//git: GIT_ASKPASS points at the tracked script that reads the mounted PAT. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 stops a failed lookup from falling back to an interactive prompt, which in an unattended run hangs until the run is killed. GIT_SSH_COMMAND=/bin/false is a second line of defence behind the missing ssh binary: even if one is added later, git cannot silently fall back to SSH.

//customizations: No postCreateCommand: the build system is plain cargo with no venv to provision. Commit identity comes from the repo's git config, as on the host.
